mainTopic: The source for liability for eating קדשים in טומאה, even without מתירין; then the new משנה on the five חטאות left to die
overview: The משנה taught that the rule against eating קדשים in טומאה applies whether or not an item has מתירין. The גמרא asks for the source and brings a ברייתא. The ברייתא first suggests a קל וחומר from פיגול: פיגול is stricter than טומאה, yet it applies only to items with מתירין, so טומאה should be limited too. A פסוק in ויקרא 22:3 rejects this and includes all קדשים. The ברייתא then asks when liability begins and points to the words "אשר יקרב". רבי אלעזר explains that items with מתירין make one liable once the מתירין are offered, and items without מתירין make one liable once they are made holy in a כלי. The chapter חטאת העוף then ends. A new משנה lists the five חטאות that are left to die, and gives the rules for a lost חטאת found blemished after the owner was already atoned for.

steps.title: What is the source for the משנה's rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the משנה's rule that טומאה applies even to items without מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the משנה's rule comes from. This question sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said one is liable for eating קדשים in טומאה whether or not the item has מתירין. The גמרא wants a source in the פסוקים for including items with no מתירין.

keyTerms.meaning: From where are these things known? The standard request for a source.
The Talmudic discussion that explains the משנה
Our משנה, the text being explained

phrases.english: Gemara: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: "These matters" means the משנה's rule that טומאה applies whether or not the item has מתירין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for liability for טומאה even on items without מתירין

steps.title: The ברייתא raises a possible limit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא opens with a possible thought: maybe one is liable for טומאה only on items that have מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Sages taught: You might have thought that one is liable for eating in טומאה only with an item that has permitting factors.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא first suggests a wrong idea, so that it can knock it down later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יכול means "you might think". It signals a mistaken idea that the ברייתא will later reject. The suggestion is that טומאה, like פיגול, is limited to items with מתירין, such as an animal offering whose blood must be sprinkled before the meat may be eaten.

keyTerms.meaning: "You might have thought". It introduces an idea that will be rejected.
Ritual impurity. Here it means eating קדשים while impure.
Permitting factors, an act (like sprinkling the blood) that makes the קרבן allowed
Liable, meaning punishable (here with כרת or a קרבן)

steps.confusionAlert: This opening line is NOT the final halacha. It is a suggestion that the ברייתא will reject in step 5.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
One might have thought one is not liable due to impurity
except for an item that has permitting factors?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the request for a source by starting the ברייתא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is a ברייתא, which begins by raising a possible limit on טומאה

steps.title: The קל וחומר begins: פיגול is strict, yet limited
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא builds a קל וחומר. פיגול is strict in three ways, yet it applies only to items with מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is logical: If פיגול, which needs only one awareness, has a fixed קרבן, and was never permitted in any situation, still applies only to an item that has permitting factors...
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a logical argument to support the suggestion in step 2. This line is the first half, describing פיגול. The second half comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: פיגול is strict in three ways. One awareness of the sin is enough to require a קרבן, the קרבן is a fixed חטאת, and it is never permitted. Even so, the איסור of פיגול applies only to items with מתירין.

keyTerms.meaning: "And it is logical". It introduces a reasoned argument.
An argument from a stricter case to a more lenient one (or the reverse)
A קרבן made unfit by improper intent about when it will be eaten
One awareness, knowing about the sin only afterward
A fixed offering, the same for rich and poor
Its general איסור was permitted in some situation

phrases.english: And it is a logical inference:
If פיגול, which is with one awareness,
and its offering is fixed,
and it was not permitted from its general rule,
phrases.notes: There is never a situation where eating פיגול is allowed.

phrases.aramaic: אֵין חַיָּיבִין אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין,
phrases.english: one is liable only for an item that has permitting factors,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind the possible limit raised in step 2
steps.raayaObject: That טומאה applies only to items with מתירין
steps.raayaSupportSource: קל וחומר from פיגול, the stricter case

steps.title: The קל וחומר concludes: טומאה is more lenient
steps.stepSummary: טומאה is more lenient than פיגול in all three ways, so it should surely be limited to items with מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...then טומאה, which needs two awarenesses, has a sliding-scale קרבן, and was permitted in some situations, is it not logical that one should be liable only for an item that has permitting factors?!
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes the קל וחומר by comparing the more lenient case, טומאה, to פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For טומאה, one must have known about the impurity before and after the sin, the קרבן is עולה ויורד (it depends on what one can afford), and טומאה is sometimes permitted for the community. Since טומאה is lighter on every point, it seems it should be at least as limited as פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Two awarenesses, knowing before the sin and again after it
A sliding-scale offering that depends on one's wealth
"Is it not logical?" This closes the קל וחומר.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the ברייתא's main point: the קל וחומר sounds strong, but a פסוק will override it.

phrases.english: impurity, which is with two awarenesses,
and its offering goes up and down,
phrases.notes: This is the sliding-scale קרבן: a wealthy person brings an animal, and a poor person brings birds or flour.

phrases.english: and it was permitted from its general rule,
phrases.notes: Communal offerings may sometimes be brought in טומאה.

phrases.english: is it not logical that one should not be liable

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל דָּבָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ מַתִּירִין?!
phrases.english: except for an item that has permitting factors?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קל וחומר begun in step 3
steps.raayaObject: That טומאה applies only to items with מתירין
steps.raayaSupportSource: טומאה is more lenient than פיגול in three ways

steps.title: The פסוק includes all קדשים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר. The פסוק about eating in טומאה speaks about all קדשים, with or without מתירין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: "Say to them: throughout your generations, any man of all your seed who approaches..." The verse speaks of all the holy items.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר with a פסוק that covers every kind of קדשים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of the קדשים in general, without limiting the rule to items with מתירין. A clear פסוק beats a logical argument. This is the source the גמרא asked for in step 1.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches". It brings a פסוק to settle the matter.
Holy items, consecrated offerings
The verse is speaking about
"Etc." The rest of the פסוק continues.

steps.whatToRemember: The rule against eating in טומאה applies to ALL קדשים, even items without מתירין. The פסוק overrides the קל וחומר from פיגול.

phrases.english: The verse states:
"Say to them: throughout your generations,
any man who approaches
of all your seed, etc."
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: "to the קדשים... while his impurity is upon him."

phrases.english: The verse is speaking of all the holy items.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of steps 3–4 using a פסוק
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole suggestion that טומאה is limited to items with מתירין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The פסוק's general wording covers all קדשים, so logic cannot narrow it
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: טומאה applies to all קדשים, which answers the source question of step 1

steps.title: Does liability start right away?
steps.stepSummary: Since all קדשים are included, the ברייתא asks whether one is liable as soon as the item becomes holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think one should be liable for them immediately?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that every קדשים item is included, the ברייתא asks a new question: from what point does liability begin? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Including items without מתירין raises a timing problem. There is no sprinkling to mark when such an item becomes "active", so maybe liability starts the moment it is consecrated.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, as soon as the item is made holy
One would be liable for them
Consecration, the act of making something holy

phrases.english: One might have thought one is liable for them immediately?
phrases.notes: "Immediately" means from the moment the item is declared holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows up on the wide inclusion of step 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When liability for eating קדשים in טומאה begins

steps.title: The words "אשר יקרב" limit the timing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words "אשר יקרב", which show that liability does not start immediately.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the timing question with two words from the same פסוק. Next, רבי אלעזר, still inside the ברייתא, explains how these words teach the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word יקרב (approaches or is brought near) is read as setting a starting point for liability, so it does not begin at the moment of consecration. At first glance the word is puzzling, because it seems to speak of touching. רבי אלעזר's words in the ברייתא (steps 8 and 9) work out exactly what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: "Who approaches" or "that is brought near", the key words of the דרשה
Approaching or offering. It is the root of יקרב.
Learning a law from the wording of a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume you already know what "אשר יקרב" teaches. The ברייתא only quotes it here, and the explanation comes right after.

phrases.english: The verse states: "Who approaches."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the timing question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words "אשר יקרב" show that liability is not immediate. The details are explained in what follows.

steps.title: Touching alone cannot make someone liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר rejects reading 'יקרב' as 'touches', because no one is liable just for touching קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Is there really someone who just touches and is liable?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר pushes back on a simple reading of the פסוק's word 'יקרב' as 'comes close' or 'touches'. This sets up his own explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא used 'אשר יקרב' to show that liability does not start right away. Reading 'יקרב' as 'touches' makes no sense, because the punishment is for eating in טומאה, not touching. So the word must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: One who touches
Literally 'comes near'; the word from the פסוק being explained
'But is it really so?' A rhetorical opener that means 'of course not'

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think touching קדשים while טמא carries this punishment. רבי אלעזר's whole point is that it does not, so the word 'יקרב' must mean something else.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
But is there one who touches who is liable?!
phrases.notes: He's reacting to 'אשר יקרב' in ויקרא 22:3. Read simply, it sounds like 'whoever comes close'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines how the word 'יקרב' from step 7 should be read
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'יקרב' as physical touching or coming near
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no liability for merely touching, so that reading cannot be what the פסוק means

steps.title: When liability begins, with and without מתירין
steps.stepSummary: With מתירין, one is liable once the מתירין are offered. Without מתירין, one is liable once the item is made holy in a כלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: So how does it work? Anything that has מתירין: one is not liable until the מתירין are offered. Anything that has no מתירין: one is not liable until it is made holy in a כלי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives the final rule of the ברייתא for exactly when the punishment for eating קדשים in טומאה starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יקרב' is understood as 'fit to be offered'. Items with מתירין count as fit once the מתירין, like the blood, have been offered. Items with no מתירין count as fit once they are made holy in a holy כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: The parts of the עבודה, like the blood, that allow the קרבן to be eaten or offered
'That they be offered', the new reading of 'יקרב'
That it becomes holy by being placed in a holy כלי
'So how is it?' It introduces the correct explanation

steps.whatToRemember: The טומאה punishment covers all קדשים. It starts once the מתירין are offered, or, if there are no מתירין, once the item is made holy in a כלי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the ברייתא's argument. The rejected קל וחומר had limited the rule to items with מתירין. The final rule includes every type of קדשים, each with its own starting point.

phrases.english: So how is this?
Any item that has permitting factors,
one is not liable until the permitting factors are offered,
phrases.notes: Here 'יקרב' is read as 'be offered', not 'come close'.

phrases.english: and any item that has no permitting factors,
one is not liable until it is sanctified in a vessel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after step 8 rejected the 'touching' reading
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Liability for eating קדשים in טומאה applies to all קדשים. It starts when the מתירין are offered, or, for items without מתירין, when the item is made holy in a כלי.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק חטאת העוף
steps.stepSummary: The closing line of the chapter חטאת העוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, חטאת העוף.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line that marks the end of the chapter. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן tells us the discussion of פרק חטאת העוף is finished. A new chapter with a new משנה starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you', said when finishing a chapter
A bird חטאת; also the name of the chapter just finished

phrases.english: We will return to you, Chattat HaOf (the bird sin offering)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter after the final ברייתא

steps.title: Three חטאות that are left to die
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה says that the offspring of a חטאת, a תמורה of a חטאת, and a חטאת whose owner died are left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: The offspring of a חטאת, the substitute of a חטאת, and a חטאת whose owners died: they are left to die.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter opens with a משנה. It lists three kinds of חטאת animals that cannot be offered and are simply left to die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: None of these animals can be offered as a חטאת, yet they are holy, so they can't just be used normally. The משנה's answer is that they are left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring born to a חטאת animal
An animal someone tried to swap for a חטאת, which becomes holy too
A חטאת whose owner died before it was offered
'They shall die', left to die rather than offered or used

phrases.english: The offspring of a sin offering, and the substitute of a sin offering,
and a sin offering whose owners have died: they shall die,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַד חַטָּאת, וּתְמוּרַת חַטָּאת, וְחַטָּאת שֶׁמֵּתוּ בְּעָלֶיהָ – יָמוּתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new chapter after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An offspring of a חטאת, a תמורה of a חטאת, and a חטאת whose owner died are all left to die.

steps.title: A lost חטאת found blemished after atonement
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds the חטאת whose year passed and the lost חטאת found blemished. If the owner has already been atoned for, it is left to die, makes no תמורה, may not be used, and carries no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one whose year passed, and one that was lost and found blemished: if this is after the owners already got atonement, it is left to die. It does not make a תמורה, one may not benefit from it, and there is no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list with two more cases. It then gives the rules for the lost-and-blemished חטאת found after the owner was already atoned for with another animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the owner has been atoned for, this animal has no purpose left. So it is left to die, and swapping another animal for it does not create a תמורה. Using it is forbidden, but if someone did use it, the law of מעילה does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Its first year has passed, too old for a חטאת
An animal with a blemish
After the owners already got atonement through another animal
Getting benefit or use from it
Being liable for מעילה, misusing הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not allowed to benefit' and 'no מעילה' are two different things. Benefiting is still forbidden from the start, but someone who did benefit does not get the מעילה penalty.
steps.whatToRemember: Five חטאות are left to die. The lost-and-blemished one found after atonement makes no תמורה, may not be used, and carries no מעילה.

phrases.english: and one whose year has passed,
and one that was lost and was found blemished,
if it is after the owners achieved atonement, it shall die.
And it does not render a substitute,
and one may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for misuse.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, וְשֶׁאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of חטאות left to die and adds their rules
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A lost חטאת found blemished after the owner was atoned for is left to die. It makes no תמורה, it is forbidden to benefit from, and it carries no מעילה.
